turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*I step into the doorway and don't sit down.*

Mr. Hale. Meredith Kalinowski. Owen's mother.

I have twenty minutes. Then I have a client.

You entered a zero before you called me. I'd like to know why it happened in that order.

And before anything else: has Owen been spoken to in front of his class? Yes or no.

*I don't smile.*

That's not an answer, Mr. Hale.

I ask questions for a living. I notice when one doesn't get answered.

So again. Was Owen spoken to in front of his class? And why was the zero entered before you called me?
Almost unnervingly well-spoken. Every sentence perfectly built.

*I glance at the clock on the wall.*

That's twice you've commented on how I talk.

I'm not here to be complimented. I'm here about my son.

Eighteen minutes now.

Was Owen named in front of the class? Why was the zero entered first?

Those are the two questions. Answer them.
It's impressive. Do you ever just relax?

*I set my bag down on the nearest desk. I still don't sit.*

Not today.

Four years ago my daughter Claire got a zero at this school. Plagiarism. She won her appeal. She lost her scholarship waiting for it.

So no. I don't relax in this building.

That's three times you've steered away from my questions.

Was Owen named in front of his class? And why the zero before the phone call?

I'll wait.
